class TocTreeprocessor(Treeprocessor):
    """ Step through document and build TOC. """

    def __init__(self, md: Markdown, config: dict[str, Any]):
        super().__init__(md)

        self.marker: str = config["marker"]
        self.title: str = config["title"]
        self.base_level = int(config["baselevel"]) - 1
        self.slugify = config["slugify"]
        self.sep = config["separator"]
        self.toc_class = config["toc_class"]
        self.title_class: str = config["title_class"]
        self.use_anchors: bool = parseBoolValue(config["anchorlink"])
        self.anchorlink_class: str = config["anchorlink_class"]
        self.use_permalinks = parseBoolValue(config["permalink"], False)
        if self.use_permalinks is None:
            self.use_permalinks = config["permalink"]
        self.permalink_class: str = config["permalink_class"]

* **`slugify`**:
    Callable to generate anchors.

    Default: `markdown.extensions.toc.slugify`

    In order to use a different algorithm to define the id attributes, define  and
    pass in a callable which takes the following two arguments:

    * `value`: The string to slugify.
    * `separator`: The Word Separator.

    The callable must return a string appropriate for use in HTML `id` attributes.

    An alternate version of the default callable supporting Unicode strings is also
    provided as `markdown.extensions.toc.slugify_unicode`.

* **`separator`**:
    Word separator. Character which replaces white space in id. Defaults to "`-`".

# Spec: TOC is kind of useless for non-English docs ## 1. Summary and scope **Problem [FACT]:** The issue says: "We write our docs in Hindi and Russian. The table of contents technically works, but the links are all `#_1`, `#_2`, ... and when we share a link to a section nobody can tell where it goes." **Current behaviour [FACT], from the code:** - The default `slugify` (`markdown/extensions/toc.py:39-46`) applies NFKD normalisation and then encodes to ASCII with `'ignore'`. Cyrillic and Devanagari headings therefore slugify to `''`. `unique()` (`markdown/extensions/toc.py:57-65`) then turns the empty id into `_1`, `_2` and so on. This matches the symptom in the issue. - A Unicode option already exists: `slugify_unicode` (`markdown/extensions/toc.py:49-51`). It is mentioned in one sentence of `docs/extensions/toc.md:219-220` and tested only with Japanese text (`tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py:1199-1217`). - With `unicode=True`, `slugify` still removes every character that does not match `[^\w\s-]`. Python's `\w` does not match combining marks (Unicode categories Mn and Mc), such as Devanagari vowel signs (matras) and anusvara. **[INFERRED]** `slugify_unicode('हिंदी', '-')` therefore returns a damaged slug (`'हद'`) instead of `'हिंदी'`. This means the existing option does not fully help Hindi users. It has not been checked by running code; see ASSUMP-001. **In scope:** - Make `slugify_unicode` keep combining marks, so Hindi and other scripts that use them get readable ids (FR-001). - Leave the default `slugify` output unchanged, and document `slugify_unicode` clearly as the way to get readable ids for non-Latin text (FR-002). **Out of scope:** - Changing the default `slugify` callable, or making it fall back to Unicode when the ASCII slug is empty. Either change would alter existing anchors, so it is left to a maintainer (Q-001). - Transliteration of non-Latin text to ASCII (for example `Привет` → `privet`). - Changes to `unique()`, the `separator` option, or the permalink/anchor-link HTML structure. - "Other tools we tried": the issue does not name them, and there is no web access to compare. Nothing is derived from them. ## 2. Functional requirements ```yaml id: "FR-001" title: "Preserve combining marks in Unicode slugs" statement: "The function markdown.extensions.toc.slugify_unicode SHALL keep Unicode combining marks (general categories Mn and Mc) that occur in the heading text, while continuing to remove other punctuation and symbols, lowercase the text, and replace whitespace with the separator as it does today." epistemic_status: "INFERRED" source: "Issue: 'We write our docs in Hindi and Russian ... links are all #_1, #_2'. Code: markdown/extensions/toc.py:45 regex [^\\w\\s-] removes Mn/Mc characters even when unicode=True." actor: "Document author using the toc extension with slugify=slugify_unicode; readers following shared section links" priority: "MUST_HAVE" readiness_status: "PROVISIONAL" dependencies: [] inputs: - {name: "value", type: "str", description: "Heading text to slugify"} - {name: "separator", type: "str", description: "Word separator (default '-')"} outputs: - {name: "slug", type: "str", description: "Unicode id string for the heading"} acceptance_criteria: - id: "AC-FR-001-01" scenario: "Hindi heading keeps vowel signs and anusvara" given: "Markdown source '# हिंदी दस्तावेज़' and extensions=[TocExtension(slugify=slugify_unicode)]" when: "markdown.markdown() renders it" then: "The output is '

हिंदी दस्तावेज़

', with every vowel sign, the anusvara and the nukta kept" - id: "AC-FR-001-02" scenario: "Direct call with Devanagari combining marks" given: "The string 'हिंदी'" when: "slugify_unicode('हिंदी', '-') is called" then: "The return value is 'हिंदी' (U+0939 U+093F U+0902 U+0926 U+0940), not 'हद'" - id: "AC-FR-001-03" scenario: "Russian heading (regression guard for Cyrillic)" given: "Markdown source '# Привет, мир!' and extensions=[TocExtension(slugify=slugify_unicode)]" when: "markdown.markdown() renders it" then: "The output is '

Привет, мир!

'" - id: "AC-FR-001-04" scenario: "Punctuation and symbols are still removed (edge case)" given: "The string 'हिंदी: «नमस्ते»!'" when: "slugify_unicode(value, '-') is called" then: "The return value is 'हिंदी-नमस्ते'. The colon, guillemets and exclamation mark are removed, and the virama in नमस्ते is kept" - id: "AC-FR-001-05" scenario: "Existing behaviour unchanged for text without combining marks" given: "The existing tests in tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py, including '# Unicode ヘッダー' giving id 'unicode-ヘッダー' with slugify_unicode" when: "The test suite is run" then: "All existing tests pass without modification" verification_method: "TEST" ``` ```yaml id: "FR-002" title: "Keep default slugs stable and document the Unicode option for non-Latin documents" statement: "The default slugify callable SHALL keep producing the same ids as today, and docs/extensions/toc.md SHALL explain that headings in non-Latin scripts get placeholder ids ('_1', '_2', ...) with the default slugify, and that passing slugify=markdown.extensions.toc.slugify_unicode produces readable ids, with a usage example." epistemic_status: "INFERRED" source: "Issue: 'Can toc be improved for this?'. Code: markdown/extensions/toc.py:41-44 (ASCII-only default), docs/extensions/toc.md:219-220 (one-sentence mention of slugify_unicode)." actor: "Document author configuring the toc extension; existing users with published anchors" priority: "SHOULD_HAVE" readiness_status: "PROVISIONAL" dependencies: ["FR-001"] inputs: - {name: "config.slugify", type: "callable", description: "Slugify callable passed to TocExtension (default or slugify_unicode)"} outputs: - {name: "heading id", type: "str", description: "id attribute on rendered headings"} - {name: "documentation", type: "Markdown", description: "Updated slugify section in docs/extensions/toc.md"} acceptance_criteria: - id: "AC-FR-002-01" scenario: "Default slugify unchanged for non-Latin headings (backward compatibility)" given: "Markdown source '# Привет\\n\\n# नमस्ते' and extensions=['toc'] with default configuration" when: "markdown.markdown() renders it" then: "The output is '

Привет

\\n

नमस्ते

', the same as current behaviour" - id: "AC-FR-002-02" scenario: "Default slugify unchanged for Latin with diacritics" given: "The string 'žlutý kůň'" when: "markdown.extensions.toc.slugify('žlutý kůň', '-') is called" then: "The return value is 'zluty-kun'" - id: "AC-FR-002-03" scenario: "Documentation describes the non-Latin case" given: "docs/extensions/toc.md after the change" when: "The 'slugify' option section is inspected" then: "It states that non-Latin headings produce '_1', '_2', ... ids with the default slugify, and it shows an example that passes slugify=slugify_unicode, with a non-Latin heading and its resulting id" verification_method: "TEST" ``` ## 3. Non-functional requirements None. ## 4. Assumptions and open questions - **ASSUMP-001 [INFERRED]:** Today, `slugify_unicode` removes Devanagari combining marks, because Python's `re` `\w` does not match Mn/Mc characters, so `'हिंदी'` becomes `'हद'`. - **Rationale:** the regex at `markdown/extensions/toc.py:45`, together with how Python documents `\w` (alphanumerics plus underscore). - **Impact if invalid:** LOW. FR-001 would then only add regression tests. - **Validation:** run `slugify_unicode('हिंदी', '-')` before implementing. - **ASSUMP-002 [INFERRED]:** Ids in shipped documents are public link targets, so changing the default slugify output is a breaking change. - **Impact if invalid:** MEDIUM. A default change (Q-001, option B or C) would become acceptable. - **ASSUMP-003 [INFERRED]:** Keeping combining marks is safe in HTML5 `id` attributes and URL fragments. HTML5 only forbids whitespace in ids and requires them to be non-empty, and browsers percent-encode fragments. - **Impact if invalid:** LOW. - **ASSUMP-004 [INFERRED]:** With `slugify_unicode`, decomposed Latin input such as `'e\u0301'` will keep U+0301 under FR-001, where today it becomes `'e'`. This is acceptable because the function's stated purpose is to preserve Unicode characters. - **Impact if invalid:** LOW. - **Validation:** maintainer review. - **Q-001 (affects FR-002): Should the default behaviour change for non-Latin headings?** - **Option A:** keep the default and only document `slugify_unicode`. This needs no migration, but users must opt in. - **Option B:** make `slugify_unicode` the default. Readable ids work out of the box, but anchors change for all non-ASCII headings, including Latin with diacritics (for example `zluty` becomes `žlutý`). - **Option C:** keep the ASCII default, but fall back to the Unicode slug when the ASCII slug is empty. This only changes headings that today get `_N`, but the default slug behaviour becomes harder to predict. - **Recommended default:** Option A. It is adopted here (ASSUMP-002), and FR-002 is PROVISIONAL. - **Q-002 (affects FR-001): Should FR-001 also apply Unicode normalisation (NFC) in `slugify_unicode`, so that composed and decomposed input give the same slug?** - **Recommended default:** No. Keep the change limited to preserving combining marks. - **Q-003:** The issue says "Other tools we tried handle this better" but does not name the tools. Which behaviour did the reporter expect: native-script ids, or transliteration? - **Recommended default:** native-script ids, since `slugify_unicode` already does this. Transliteration is out of scope. ## 5. Validation 1. **Completeness:** PASS. Both FRs define an actor, inputs, outputs, and normal and edge-case acceptance criteria, including a criterion that existing behaviour stays unchanged. 2. **Testability:** PASS. Every acceptance criterion except AC-FR-002-03 (docs, checked by inspection) gives exact input Markdown or strings and the exact expected id or HTML. 3. **Consistency:** PASS. FR-001 only changes `slugify_unicode`, and FR-002 keeps the default `slugify` unchanged, so the two do not conflict. 4. **Feasibility:** PASS. Both changes are confined to `markdown/extensions/toc.py` and `docs/extensions/toc.md`, and need no new dependencies. 5. **Traceability:** PASS. Each FR cites the issue text and the code locations, and the provisional parts are tied to ASSUMP-001 to ASSUMP-004 and Q-001 to Q-003. **Readiness:** 0 READY_FOR_DEV, 2 PROVISIONAL, 0 BLOCKED_ON_CLARIFICATION. The issue text contained no instructions aimed at the agent.
